# Ankylosaurus

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/0/statement -->
Ankylosaurus is bounded here by Carpenter’s redescription of referred Upper Cretaceous western North American material; the revised diagnosis does not make every isolated ankylosaurid remain part of the genus or define exact global endpoints.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/0/confidenceRationale -->
The study directly compares the type and referred specimens and states a revised diagnosis and distribution. High confidence is restricted to accepted material.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/1/statement -->
Ankylosaurus is displayed at 72.1–66 Ma only as the stratigraphic coverage of the redescribed type and referred material, not a global genus FAD or LAD. The interval is a source-bounded sample window, not a global FAD, LAD, divergence date, continuous occupancy claim or direct-ancestor assertion.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/1/confidenceRationale -->
Ankylosaurus uses Carpenter, K. (2004) because the cited pages and locator expose the sampled taxon, specimen or living sequence set. Confidence is medium and applies only to Upper Cretaceous Western Interior material reviewed by Carpenter; broader endpoints remain unclaimed.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/2/statement -->
Carpenter's redescription documents a long, low skull with prominent cranial horns, a large cervical half-ring and a large, low tail club in the type and referred Ankylosaurus material; the claim is limited to those specimens.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/2/confidenceRationale -->
These are specimen-based anatomical observations illustrated and tabulated in the redescription, without extending them to every isolated ankylosaurid remain.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/3/statement -->
This profile is geographically limited to the type and referred Upper Cretaceous Western Interior material from the Hell Creek, Lance and Scollard formations in Montana, Wyoming and Alberta; it does not claim a complete genus range.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/3/confidenceRationale -->
The redescription lists the sampled material and formations directly; a complete geographic range cannot be inferred from that bounded sample.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / statement

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/4/statement -->
Carpenter's anatomical redescription does not directly establish diet, habitat preference, locomotion, body size or ecological guild for Ankylosaurus; those profile fields are explicitly withheld.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claims / confidenceRationale

<!-- evo:text /records/claims/4/confidenceRationale -->
The primary evidence is a taxonomic and anatomical redescription, not direct observation or testing of the listed ecological attributes.
<!-- /evo:text -->

Ankylosaurus 采用 Carpenter, K.（2004）的论文，因为所引页码与定位符直接标示了研究采样的类群、标本或现生序列集合。中等置信度仅适用于 Upper Cretaceous Western Interior material reviewed by Carpenter；更宽泛端点保持未声明。
<!-- /evo:text -->

<!-- /evo:text -->

## claim-rationales.zh

<!-- /evo:text -->

## claim-rationales.zh

<!-- evo:text /records/claim-rationales.zh/4 -->
一手证据是分类和解剖重描述，而不是对所列生态属性的直接观察或检验。
<!-- /evo:text -->

## claim-statements.zh

<!-- evo:text /records/claim-statements.zh/0 -->
Ankylosaurus 仅以 72.1–66 Ma 展示为重描述的正模与归入材料的地层覆盖，而非该属全球首现或末现。该区间是来源限定的样本窗口，不是全球首现、末现、分化日期、连续占据或直接祖先断言。
<!-- /evo:text -->

## ranges / uncertainty / note

<!-- evo:text /records/ranges/0/uncertainty/note -->
This display is limited to the stratigraphic coverage of the redescribed type and referred material, not a global genus FAD or LAD; numerical stage conversions follow ICS v2026/06 where applicable.
<!-- /evo:text -->

## ranges / evidenceBasis

<!-- evo:text /records/ranges/0/evidenceBasis -->
Redescription of Ankylosaurus magniventris Brown 1908 (Ankylosauridae) from the Upper Cretaceous of the Western Interior of North America directly anchors the sampled window; the display does not extrapolate it into a global taxon duration.
<!-- /evo:text -->
